name: PyTorch Foundation
summary: The Linux Foundation’s home for PyTorch and, since May 2025, five more AI projects: vLLM, DeepSpeed, Ray, Helion and Safetensors.
intro: The PyTorch Foundation is part of the non-profit Linux Foundation. Meta set it up on September 12, 2022 to take over PyTorch, the deep-learning framework Facebook had released in 2016, with AMD, Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, Meta, Microsoft Azure and NVIDIA on its first governing board. On May 7, 2025 it became an umbrella foundation and accepted two more projects, vLLM and DeepSpeed; Ray followed in October 2025, and Helion and Safetensors in April 2026. In October 2026 it hosted those six projects, and its PyTorch Conference in San Jose drew more than 3,500 people.

For someone choosing a technology, the badge says who holds the project. A hosted project has won a two-thirds vote of the Technical Advisory Council (TAC), and the Linux Foundation’s lawyers have taken over its assets, so the company that wrote it no longer controls it alone. Applicants must show production use, a strong and diverse contributor base, compatibility with recent PyTorch releases and the OpenSSF Best Practices silver badge, and each hosted project has a representative on the TAC.

It is not a maturity ladder. Unlike the CNCF, the foundation has no sandbox or graduated stages: the TAC files each hosted project as Platform, if it spans several stages of the AI lifecycle such as training and inference, or Vertical, if it serves one field such as protein folding, and reviews every project once a year, with retirement the only other status. The much larger PyTorch Ecosystem, more than 100 projects in February 2026 including SGLang, verl and Unsloth, is a curated list of independently governed projects, not part of the foundation.

sections.title: The six hosted projects
sections.intro: As listed on pytorch.org in October 2026. ExecuTorch, Meta’s runtime for phones and microcontrollers, became part of PyTorch core in April 2026 rather than a separate hosted project.

rows.label: PyTorch
values: The deep-learning framework; its CI costs more than $1.5 million a month, paid mostly by Meta and AWS

rows.label: vLLM
values: An inference and serving engine for large language models, built around PagedAttention

rows.label: DeepSpeed
values: A distributed training library: ZeRO, 3D parallelism and inference acceleration

rows.label: Ray
values: Distributed compute for data processing, training and inference; more than 237 million downloads when it joined

rows.label: Helion
values: A Python-embedded language for machine-learning kernels that compiles to Triton and TileIR and autotunes them

rows.label: Safetensors
values: A file format for model weights that can’t run arbitrary code when it is loaded

sections.title: Ecosystem first, then hosting
body: A project reaches the foundation in two steps. It first applies to the PyTorch Ecosystem, run by the TAC’s Ecosystem Working Group; ecosystem projects keep their own governance and appear on the PyTorch landscape, and 14 joined in 2025. Only an approved ecosystem project can then apply to be foundation-hosted, through an issue in the `pytorch-fdn/foundation-hosted` repository, with a voting TAC member as its sponsor.

The TAC reviews the application at one of its monthly meetings and needs a two-thirds majority to accept it. A declined project stays in the ecosystem and may reapply after three months if it has made tangible progress. After a yes, the Linux Foundation’s legal team completes the contribution and the transfer of the project’s assets, and foundation staff set up its branding, website, marketing and CI. The TAC reviews every hosted project each year and can retire one that has gone inactive or stopped meeting the requirements.

sections.title: Who decides
body: Business and technical decisions are split. The Governing Board runs the foundation under its charter: each top-tier member appoints a representative, the other paying members elect up to three between them, and the TAC has a seat. The foundation updated its membership tiers by February 2026, when it had 33 member organisations, and nine more joined at the October 2026 conference, with Nebius, Nscale and Shopify as Platinum members.

The TAC is the technical body. In October 2026 its 21 members included a representative of each hosted project, among them Meta for PyTorch, Inferact for vLLM, Snowflake for DeepSpeed, Anyscale for Ray and Hugging Face for Safetensors, alongside engineers from members such as AMD, Arm, Google, Huawei, Intel, Microsoft and NVIDIA; Thomas Viehmann of Lightning AI chairs it. It runs five working groups: CI infrastructure, multi-cloud, ecosystem, accelerators and security. Each project keeps its own maintainers and technical governance; PyTorch’s is written down by its maintainers.

Paid staff run the rest. In February 2026 Matt White, executive director for nearly two years, became the foundation’s CTO, and Mark Collier, a co-founder of OpenStack, took over as executive director, in charge of finances, events, staff and membership.

story: Facebook released PyTorch in 2016, and by 2022 it had more than 2,400 contributors. On September 12, 2022 Meta moved it to a new foundation at the Linux Foundation, with the companies whose chips and clouds it ran on, AMD, AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure and NVIDIA, on the board beside Meta. For two and a half years the foundation hosted only PyTorch, while a list of ecosystem projects built on it grew to about 120.

On May 7, 2025, at PyTorch Day France in Paris, it announced that it would become an umbrella foundation, with vLLM and DeepSpeed as its first new hosted projects; it then had more than 30 member companies. Ray joined at the PyTorch Conference in San Francisco on October 22, 2025, putting model development, inference and distributed execution under one foundation. Sixteen companies joined as members that year.

In February 2026 Mark Collier replaced Matt White as executive director. At the first PyTorch Conference Europe, in Paris on April 7 and 8, 2026, Meta contributed Helion and Hugging Face contributed Safetensors, and ExecuTorch became part of PyTorch core. In October 2026 Nscale, which plans to buy Ray’s developer Anyscale, joined as a Platinum member.

choices.choice: A Linux Foundation project, not a Meta one
choices.why: PyTorch ran on chips and clouds sold by Meta’s partners and competitors, so its first board seated AMD, AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure and NVIDIA beside Meta, with the Linux Foundation holding the project.

choices.choice: An umbrella for the AI stack
choices.why: Projects such as vLLM and DeepSpeed were already built on PyTorch, and the foundation wanted a vendor-neutral home for projects across the AI lifecycle, from training and inference to agents, not only for the framework.

Ecosystem projects keep their own governance and only get listed; hosted projects adopt the foundation’s governance and get full operational support. Requiring ecosystem status first means the TAC already knows a project before it takes on its assets.

choices.choice: Categories by scope, not by maturity
choices.why: The umbrella was set up for Platform projects that span several stages of the AI lifecycle and Vertical projects for fields such as bioinformatics, geospatial intelligence and protein folding, so the TAC classifies projects by what they cover rather than ranking them.
